subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A common business objective for a brand-new start-up is most likely to be:
questions.explain: Survival is a key short-term objective for new businesses, which often face high failure rates early on.

questions.q: The recruitment process usually begins with:
options: Identifying a vacancy and producing a job description
questions.explain: Recruitment starts by identifying a vacancy and writing a job description and person specification.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of primary market research?
options: Carrying out a customer survey yourself
questions.explain: Primary research is first-hand data collected directly, such as a survey carried out by the business itself.

questions.q: Which of the following lists the 4 Ps of the marketing mix?
questions.explain: The marketing mix is made up of Product, Price, Place and Promotion.

questions.q: An advantage of internal recruitment is that:
options: It always brings in fresh ideas from outside
It avoids the need for training
It guarantees a larger pool of applicants
The candidate is already known to the business and it is usually cheaper
questions.explain: Internal recruitment is cheaper and the applicant is already known, though it may limit fresh ideas.

questions.q: What is the main role of an entrepreneur when starting a business?
options: To take a risk by organising resources to set up a business
To work only as an employee for a larger firm
To guarantee the business will make a profit
questions.explain: An entrepreneur takes the risk of combining resources (land, labour, capital) to create a new business.

questions.q: Why might shareholders and employees have conflicting interests?
options: Neither group cares about the business
Both want the business to close
Shareholders may want higher profits while employees want higher wages
questions.explain: Higher wages can reduce profits, so shareholders' and employees' interests can conflict.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a stakeholder in a business?
questions.explain: Stakeholders are any groups with an interest in the business, including employees, customers and suppliers.

questions.q: Which type of business ownership is owned by its shareholders but cannot sell shares to the general public?
questions.explain: A private limited company (Ltd) is owned by shareholders but its shares cannot be sold to the public.

questions.q: Which is an example of a non-financial method of motivation?
questions.explain: Job rotation and added responsibility motivate without extra pay, so they are non-financial methods.

questions.q: Which statement about a sole trader is correct?
options: They have unlimited liability for business debts
questions.explain: A sole trader has unlimited liability, meaning personal assets are at risk if the business cannot pay its debts.

questions.q: In a partnership, profits are usually:
questions.explain: Partners typically share the profits (and losses) of the business according to their agreement.
